result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers drop the 18% figure and the Hartwell Metals claim. Both build the pitch on true points: the contingency-only fee, the founders' billing background, and a free look at a few months of invoices. B wins narrowly because its final email makes replying very easy ('just reply "interested"') and its first email has a single ask, while A's first email offers both a call and an invoice sample. A's first follow-up adds a new point about why in-house teams miss billing errors, but its explanation of why it dropped the claims leans slightly toward a lecture. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers drop the 18% figure and the Hartwell Metals claim, and both build on what the brief supports: the contingency fee, the founders' carrier-billing background and a low-risk invoice sample. B's first follow-up adds a new point (billing errors are rarely caught in-house) as well as making it easier to reply, and its final email leaves the door open cleanly. A's first follow-up mixes the invoice offer with a call ask. B's first email does offer two options, and its refusal runs a little long.
